### P1 — Toolbar alignment is not optional

Both right-aligned toolbars must terminate on the same x-coordinate: 4pt from the card’s inner trailing edge. Do not align their glyphs by eye; align their 28pt hit-target frames.

### P1 — Divider treatment is ambiguous

The current header intentionally has no bottom rule, but making it permanent places two chrome rows directly together.

Fix:

- Add a 1-device-pixel `tokens.border` rule below the pane header.
- Run it from 8pt leading inset to 4pt trailing inset.
- Keep the terminal tab strip’s own separators unchanged.
- Between the action group and Remove from Split, use a 1px × 14pt divider with 6pt on each side.
- Keep split-resize gutters visually empty; the pane-edge focus stroke supplies the boundary. Do not add another rule inside the inter-pane gap.

## 4. Focus signalling

### P0 — The proposed focus treatment is overloaded

The focused pane would have:

- Accent card fill.
- Accent glyph.
- Bright header text.
- Accessibility `isSelected`.
- A selected titlebar chip.
- Existing terminal focus treatment.

That is five visual/model signals for one state, and the titlebar chip already communicates the selected workroom.

The single best in-content signal is a 1-device-pixel focus ring around the pane, using the accessible accent-derived stroke only while the window is key.

Concrete fix:

- Remove accent card fill.
- Remove focused shadow changes.
- Keep header text at normal primary/secondary hierarchy in all panes.
- Keep identity glyph semantic—house/cube or VCS state—not focus-colored.
- Draw one inset 1px focus ring around the active pane.
- Retain `.isSelected` only when there are multiple visible panes.

This remains visible around terminal content without competing with it.

## 5. Accessibility

### P0 — Accent-at-10% is not an accessible selection mechanism

It has no guaranteed contrast in light themes or custom palettes.

Fix: selection must remain recognizable without color or translucency. Use the 1px ≥3:1 focus stroke, plus `.isSelected` for multi-pane accessibility. Do not require users to perceive the fill.

### P0 — Focus tint must be key-window aware

Fix: combine pane model focus with window key state. Inactive windows get neutral borders and no accent focus treatment. Accessibility selection may remain reported, but VoiceOver labels should not imply keyboard focus unless that pane actually owns it.

### P1 — Every new control needs a tooltip and stable label

Required tooltips:

- Open in {editor}, including shortcut.
- Choose editor.
- Run, Stop, Restart, including shortcuts.
- Configure Run when unavailable.
- No supported editor installed.
- More actions.
- Remove from Split.
- Missing-directory warning.
- Project-root/workroom identity when truncated.

Add stable identifiers to both Open In controls and the overflow control. The title itself needs a tooltip containing the full label and path when truncated.

### P0 — Non-focused pane actions are not keyboard reachable

Moving Run per pane fixes pointer targeting but does not create a keyboard model. `⌘R` still operates on selection, and there is no direct keyboard route to a non-focused split member.

Fix:

- Add `⌃Tab` / `⌃⇧Tab` to cycle focus among visible workroom panes in spatial order.
- Once focused, existing `⌘R`, `⇧⌘R`, `⌥⌘R`, and `⇧⌘O` operate on that pane.
- Announce “Focused pane: {project}, {workroom}” through accessibility.
- Button activation must first focus its owning pane, then execute against its explicit target.
- Header buttons must participate in Full Keyboard Access with a predictable order: identity, Run/Stop, Restart, Open In, overflow, Remove.

Do not invent separate shortcuts for every visible Run button; establish pane focus, then reuse the existing command vocabulary.

## 6. The ambiguity that will haunt implementation

### P0 — The unresolved width-pressure policy will cause the most lasting damage

If the plan does not define which controls persist, which collapse, and which labels truncate at exact widths, every developer and test will encode a different assumption. It affects:

- SwiftUI layout priority.
- Toolbar identity and spacing.
- Overflow behavior.
- Accessibility order.
- Snapshot tests.
- Localization.
- Split minimum widths.
- Solo-versus-split geometry.

The plan must include the numerical responsive contract above before implementation starts. The runner-up is focus semantics, but width pressure will infect more files and be substantially harder to unwind later.

My strongest recommendation: keep the per-pane action ownership, reject the always-visible duplicate solo identity header, replace accent cards with one accessible focus ring, and specify the 320pt/240pt responsive transitions before code is changed.

# Issue #139 — Always show the workroom title bar and toolbar

## Context

Today a workroom only gets its own chrome when it is part of a **split group**. `WorkroomPaneLeaf`
(`macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:140`) gates a header + card underlay behind
`multi` (`leaves.count >= 2`, line 51): a `project / workroom` title bar with the remove-from-split
✕, and a rounded, tinted, shadowed card beneath the whole pane. A solo workroom gets none of it —
its terminal tab strip sits bare at the top of the detail area.

Meanwhile the workroom's own actions live in the **window titlebar**: `TrailingTitlebarBar`
(`Views/TitlebarBars.swift:162-169`) renders `OpenInControl` + `RunControls` keyed on
`store.selectedTarget`. That is the wrong home twice over:

- **Workroom-scoped controls in window-scoped chrome.** In a split every visible member has a path
  and a run state, but only the *selected* one is reachable.
- **`store.runOrFocusRunCommand()` reads the selection**, so a per-member Run button would start the
  run in the wrong workroom. That is a real semantic bug, not just placement.

Outcome: every workroom, split or not, renders as a self-contained card with its own title bar and
its own trailing toolbar; the window titlebar keeps only global chrome. Because the header becomes
unconditional, `WorkroomPaneLeaf` **loses** most of its `multi` branching rather than gaining more —
with no `if multi` there is no `_ConditionalContent` branch to flip when a split dissolves, so the
libghostty re-parent hazard on that axis disappears outright.

## Decisions of record

| # | Decision | Note |
|---|----------|------|
| D1 | Header always on; run + Open-in leave the titlebar **entirely** and become per-workroom; titlebar keeps sidebar toggle, back/forward, workroom chips, update pill, Quick Terminal | confirmed |
| D2 | Solo card geometry **identical** to a split member — 6pt outer gutter + 4pt inset | confirmed; makes `compact` genuinely dead |
| D3 | Solo renders accent-tinted (as a focused member) | confirmed, **+ key-window awareness** (see C3 below) |
| D4 | Header toolbar keeps `ToolbarIconButtonStyle` | confirmed, **+ both toolbars' trailing edges aligned by frame** (C4) |

Four cross-model challenges were raised at the gate and resolved:

| # | Challenge | Outcome |
|---|-----------|---------|
| C1 | Use the existing `tabToolbar` instead of a new header row | **Rejected.** The header is the container workroom UI grows into; the 28pt cost is deliberate. |
| C2 | Don't repeat the chip's label solo | **Rejected.** The chip can scroll out of an overflowing tab bar; the header is the pane's reliable identity. |
| C3 | Don't tint the solo card accent | **Rejected, with the accessibility half accepted:** the tint goes neutral when the window is not key. Light-theme contrast of `accent @ 0.10` is on the manual checklist. |
| C4 | Unify on `TabToolbarButton` | **Rejected, with the alignment half accepted:** keep the style, align both toolbars' trailing edges by hit-target frame and assert it. |

## The shape of the change

```
BEFORE                                    AFTER
window titlebar                           window titlebar
 ├ sidebar toggle, back/fwd                ├ sidebar toggle, back/fwd
 ├ workroom tab chips                      ├ workroom tab chips
 └ update · OpenIn · Run · QuickTerm       └ update · QuickTerm

detail (solo)          detail (split)     detail (solo AND split — one shape)
┌──────────────────┐   ┌──────┐┌──────┐   ┌────────────────────────────────┐
│ [tab][tab] +  ⧈ ⧉│   │ hdr ✕││ hdr ✕│   │ ⬛ project / room   ⏵ ⧉  [✕]  │ ← always, 28pt
│ ░░ terminal ░░░░ │   │[tab] ││[tab] │   ├────────────────────────────────┤
└──────────────────┘   │ ░░░░ ││ ░░░░ │   │ [tab][tab] +          ⧈ ⧉ ⊠   │
  no card, 2pt gutter  └──────┘└──────┘   │ ░░░ terminal ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ │
                        cards, 6+4        └────────────────────────────────┘
                                            card + 6pt outer / 4pt inset
                                            [✕] = remove-from-split, multi only
```

`multi` survives in exactly **four** leaf-level places, none structural for the terminal: the ✕, the
context menu's "Remove from Split" item, the group-drag gesture mask, and the a11y `.isSelected`
trait.

**Cost, stated deliberately:** in-content chrome above the terminal goes 30pt → 58pt solo (+93%);
split members already pay ~62pt, so solo converges on split. Terminal loses 4pt per side.

---

## Implementation

### 1. `Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift` — the header becomes unconditional

**`WorkroomPaneLeaf.body` (140-218).** Drop the `if multi` around the header (150). **Keep the
`VStack(spacing: 0) { titleBar; content }` shape exactly** — the comment at 140-148 is load-bearing;
the header must stay a sibling above `content`, never a wrapper.

- **Gesture mask — `.subviews`, never `.none`.**
  `.gesture(dragGesture, including: multi ? .all : .subviews)`.
  `GestureMask.none` disables **all gestures in the subview hierarchy including the added one**, so
  `.none` would ship the solo pane's Run and Open-in buttons **dead** — and hover would still light
  their wells (`ToolbarIconButtonStyle` uses `.onHover`, not a gesture), so they would look alive.
  There is no `GestureMask` precedent anywhere in the app to catch this. Its effect on the sibling
  `.contextMenu` and on the AppKit `Menu` popup is undocumented — **prove both by real click.**
- `.contextMenu` (182-186) stays attached always: pass `onRemoveFromSplit: multi ? onClose : nil`;
  `workroomContextMenu` already omits the item and its divider on `nil`
  (`Views/WorkroomContextMenu.swift:37,50`). Scope the menu's `.contentShape` to the **leading label
  region** and attach the same menu to the trailing group, so right-click doesn't become positional
  guesswork once the bar's right half is buttons.
- **Card modifiers (196-213): delete every `multi ?` ternary.** `panel`, `cornerRadius: 8`, the
  focused/unfocused shadow, and `EdgeInsets(4,4,4,4)` become unconditional. Solo is *always* the
  selected leaf, so `focused` is already `true` — D3's accent needs no special case.
- **Key-window awareness (C3).** Extract the fill into a small child view
  `WorkroomPaneCardBackground(focused:)` that reads `@Environment(\.controlActiveState)` and returns
  `splitGroupFocusedFill` only when the window is key, `splitGroupFill` otherwise. As a child, it
  absorbs the activation churn on its own — the leaf and the terminal subtree below never
  re-evaluate for it. (Same invalidation reasoning as `RunControls` below.)
- `content(compact: multi)` (190) → `content()`; see §3.
- **Make the missing-directory choice non-structural.** Once §6 routes solo-missing through this
  leaf, the `if target.isMissing` at 236-256 can flip **in place under a live pane** — the exact
  hazard 140-148 warns about, which solo could never hit before. Always mount
  `TargetTerminalDetail` and draw the "Directory not found" `ContentUnavailableView` as an
  **overlay** over it. Update the 140-148 comment: the header is no longer the only such hazard.
- `.accessibilityAddTraits(focused && multi ? .isSelected : [])` (217): **keep the `multi` term.**
  Solo has nothing to select between, and this trait tracks *model* focus, not first responder —
  widening it would make every solo pane report selected and break how tests read it.

**`WorkroomSplitView.body` (83).** `.padding(.horizontal, multi ? 6 : 0)` → a named
`static let outerGutter: CGFloat = 6`, applied unconditionally. §6 must subtract it from the
drop hit-test.

**`WorkroomSplitDivider` — hold the live ratio locally.** `onChanged` currently calls
`onSetRatio` per mouse-move tick → `store.setWorkroomSplitRatio` writes `@Published workroomSplits`
→ `RootView` re-evaluates → **every leaf rebuilds at mouse-move rate.** With the header now doing
real work per pane, that becomes a hot path. Track the live ratio in `WorkroomSplitView` `@State` and
commit once on `.onEnded` — exactly the pattern `SidebarColumn.swift:22-24,47-62` already uses
("so each mouse-moved tick re-renders just this column, not the whole RootView tree").

**`WorkroomSplitGroupTitleBar` (264-317) → rename `WorkroomPaneTitleBar`** (no longer split-specific).
Props become `target: TerminalTarget`, `projectPath: String?`, `workroomName: String?`,
`focused: Bool`, `multi: Bool`, `onClose`, `onFocus`. Pass `projectPath` (the leaf already computes
`AppStore.projectPath(of: sid)` for `projectLabel`) rather than `sid` — one lookup, and no
`SidebarID` dependency in a presentation view. Derive `projectLabel` from it; drop the redundant
`isMissing` prop (`target.isMissing`). Keep
`accessibilityIdentifier("workroom.pane.titlebar")` — six `SplitPaneUITests` tests query it.

- **Glyph by kind:** `workroomName == nil` means a project root → `house`, matching the chip
  (`WorkroomTabBar.swift:487`); `cube` otherwise. Drop the `"Workroom "` a11y prefix for roots.
  Rare today (split-only); unconditional it is *every* root pane.
- **Trailing run:**

```swift
Spacer(minLength: 8)
HStack(spacing: 6) {
  if !target.isMissing {
    OpenInControl(path: target.path)
    if let projectPath { RunControls(target: target, projectPath: projectPath, onFocus: onFocus) }
  }
}
.frame(width: Self.actionsWidth, alignment: .trailing)   // reserved — see §5 / responsive contract
.buttonStyle(ToolbarIconButtonStyle())
if multi {
  TitlebarDivider()
  CloseWorkroomPaneButton(action: onClose)   // brings its own .plain style
}
```

- **`RunControls`' `@EnvironmentObject var store` is safe here.** SwiftUI invalidates only the view
  that declares the dependency, so it does **not** subscribe `WorkroomPaneLeaf` or the terminal
  subtree — the invariant at `WorkroomSplitView.swift:23-26,124-127` holds.
  `TargetTerminalDetail.swift:20` already reads the same environment object inside this leaf, so this
  is established practice.
- **Extract a pure `WorkroomPaneToolbarPresentation`** (`showsOpenIn` / `showsRun` / `showsClose`
  from `isMissing` / `hasRunCommand` / `multi`) beside `WorkroomSplitTitlePresentation` (112-118), so
  the trailing block is unit-testable without instantiating a view. `WorkroomSplitTitlePresentation`
  must survive — `WorkroomAppTests/WorkroomLabelTests.swift:88` tests it.
- **Hover** must be live for `ToolbarIconButtonStyle` and the `Menu`. The detail sits inside the
  `NavigationSplitView` that exists precisely to keep `.onHover` working near the top of the content
  (`RootView.swift:174-184`, issue #114). Verify with a **real mouse** — synthetic events lie here.

### 2. `Core/AppStore.swift` — Run must act on the passed target

```swift
/// ⌘R / menu: act on the current selection. Suppressed while a text field is being edited.
func runOrFocusRunCommand() {
  guard !isEditingTextField, let target = selectedTarget else { return }
  runOrFocusRunCommand(for: target)
}

/// The per-target state machine (the diagram at 1603-1629 moves here). A workroom's own Run
/// button calls this directly with ITS target.
func runOrFocusRunCommand(for target: TerminalTarget) {
  guard !target.isMissing else { return }
  … existing switch body, unchanged …
}
```

`isEditingTextField` stays on the **selection wrapper only**. That is deliberate and fixes a latent
bug: today a Run *click* while the sidebar filter or the Project Settings command field holds focus
silently no-ops, because the guard was written for ambient ⌘R (its own comment at 1593-1597 says so).
`stopRunCommand(for:)` (1711) and `restartRunCommand(for:)` (1726) already take a target and carry no
such guard, so all three buttons become consistent. Leave `toggleRunCommand(for:)` (1583, the sidebar
row toggle) alone — different semantics.

**Raise the member on the focus branches.** `.running(_, false)`/`.restarting` calls
`terminals.focus(tab, for: target)`, which switches *that member's* active tab **without** focusing
the member — and a non-focused member renders `surfaceActive: false` and is dimmed, so pressing Run
there looks like nothing happened. Thread the leaf's `onFocus` through `RunControls` and call it
before acting, or set `selectedTargetID` in the overload when the target is a visible member.

### 3. Delete the `compact` axis (D2 makes it dead)

With solo and split geometry identical, `compact` is permanently `true`. Remove it and inline the
values — a live-looking branch that can only take one value is worse than none:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:190,235` | `content(compact:)` → `content()` |
| `Views/TargetTerminalDetail.swift:19,27` | drop `var compact` + the pass-through |
| `Views/WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:21,59-60,86` | drop `var compact`; padding becomes `.horizontal, 2` / `.bottom, 2` |
| `Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:24,63` | drop `var compact`; `leadingInset` becomes `4` |

Rewrite the comments those numbers carry (they explain the solo-vs-split difference) to state the
single rule. Two adjacent fixes while in these files:

- **`WorkroomTerminalsView`: move the gutter padding onto the outer `Group`.** The zero-tab
  "No terminal" `ContentUnavailableView` (62-74) sits *outside* the `.padding` at 59-61, so inside a
  card it would render with no inset.
- **Fix the false invariant at 131-139.** The comment claims "this view mounts only in the
  single-workroom path" — already untrue for every split member, and this change edits those lines.

### 4. `Views/TitlebarBars.swift` — the titlebar loses the workroom controls

Delete the `if let target = store.selectedTarget, !target.isMissing { … }` block (162-169) with its
`OpenInControl`, `RunControls`, and trailing `TitlebarDivider`. What remains: the update pill (+ its
divider) and Quick Terminal. Update the doc comment (140-143), which advertises "the selected
target's run/open-in actions". **Check the resulting spacing** — with no update pending the trailing
bar becomes a lone button, and this change removes a group divider.

**Nothing else moves.** The Run menu (`WorkroomApp.swift:939-949`), Go ▸ "Open in …" (1082-1086), the
`AppDelegate` ⌘R/⌥⌘R/⇧⌘R monitor (267-288), and the `hasRunCommand`/`canOpenInEditor`
`focusedSceneValue`s keep acting on the selection through the unchanged selection-scoped entry
points. The keyboard path to a non-focused member stays "focus the pane, then ⌘R" — accepted; no new
shortcuts.

### 5. `Views/TargetDetailToolbar.swift` — ids, layout stability, multi-window

- **Accessibility ids.** `OpenInControl` has none today (only dynamic labels), which is why it has
  zero UI coverage. Add `openIn.primary` and `openIn.menu` (dotted convention). `RunControls` keeps
  `runCommand.run` / `.stop` / `.restart` verbatim — six existing tests query them.
- **Reserve the trailing width.** `RunControls` renders 1 button idle and 2 running, and nothing when
  `canRunCommand` is false; `OpenInControl` renders nothing with no editor installed. That is a ~28pt
  swing at run start, which moves the identity label's truncation point mid-run. Give the group a
  fixed reserved width (Stop+Restart's) or cross-fade the two states in a `ZStack`. In-repo
  precedent: `WorkroomTabBar.swift:202-212` toggles **opacity, not presence**, for exactly this.
- **Multi-window.** `runStates` is per-store, so window B renders `Run` while window A renders
  `Stop` for the same workroom — two adjacent contradictory buttons once this is per-pane. Read
  `WindowRegistry.shared.runOwner(for:excluding:)` too and render the not-mine-but-running case as a
  "focus the owner" affordance, not a Run button that silently teleports the user.
- Update both doc comments (9-14, 67-71): the host is the workroom pane title bar now.

### 6. `Views/RootView.swift` — close the two "no header" holes, fix the hit-test

- **Delete the `if target.isMissing` branch (584-590).** A solo missing workroom never reaches
  `WorkroomSplitView` today, so "always" was false. `target(for:)` returns a target even when the
  directory is gone, so deleting this routes it through `workroomSplitBody` → `.leaf(selected)` →
  the leaf, which renders the identical `ContentUnavailableView` (see §1's non-structural overlay).
- **Creation slot (577-582):** `isCreationFocused` bypasses the pane, while a *non-focused* creating
  member **does** get a header — "pixel-identical" breaks in the opposite direction from the missing
  case. **Decision: leave the creating slot chrome-less** (the setup dialog owns that moment) and say
  so in the comment; the premise reads "every workroom with a mounted pane", not "every state".
- **Subtract the gutter in the drop math.** `workroomChipDropTarget` (556-563) plans against the
  **unpadded** `detailContentFrame`, while the renderer plans *inside* `.padding(.horizontal, 6)`.
  Solo is pixel-exact today (0 padding); unconditional 6pt makes every drop 6pt off — a drop in the
  gutter is contained by RootView's rect (so it splits) but not by the pane rect (so **no** preview
  showed first). Subtract `WorkroomSplitView.outerGutter` in `workroomChipLocal`/`workroomChipDropTarget`.
- **Dead code, adjacent to these edits:** delete the never-called `titlebarBar` (63-89) and
  `workroomSplitBody`'s unreachable `else` branch (`selectedTarget` is
  `selectedTargetID.flatMap(target(for:))`, so a non-nil target implies a non-nil id).
- Add a no-op guard to `selectWorkroomTab` (570-573) — the solo header's focus tap now fires on
  every header click and rewrites unchanged selection state, publishing a whole-tree re-render.

### 7. `Core/ExternalEditor.swift` — cache the lookup before it goes per-pane

`ExternalEditor.installed` (19-26) is an **uncached computed property** doing 3
`NSWorkspace.urlForApplication(withBundleIdentifier:)` LaunchServices lookups; `icon` (47-51) calls
`NSWorkspace.icon(forFile:)` **and mutates the returned image's `size`** (shared-state mutation on an
image `NSWorkspace` may hand out from its own cache). Today that runs once per window; after this it
runs once per visible pane, on every mount, selection change, focus change and run-state change.
Back `installed` and the icons with a static cache invalidated on
`NSWorkspace.didLaunchApplicationNotification` / `didTerminateApplicationNotification`, and copy the
image before resizing. Worth doing regardless of this issue.

---

## Responsive contract (the numbers, stated once)

Both review voices named the missing width policy as the ambiguity that would do the most lasting
damage — every developer and test would otherwise encode a different assumption.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Header height | 28pt (unchanged) |
| Identity label cap | **180pt**, matching the chip's `maxTitleWidth` (`WorkroomTabBar.swift:410`) |
| Trailing group | fixed reserved width = Stop+Restart's, so the label's truncation point is a function of pane width only |
| Toolbar trailing edge | **both** the header's group and `tabToolbar` terminate 4pt from the card's inner trailing edge, aligned by **hit-target frame** (C4) — asserted, not eyeballed |
| Card geometry | 6pt outer gutter + 4pt inset all round → card edge sits **8pt** from the sidebar card; terminal at 14pt. (Today: terminal at 10pt. The draft's "10pt to the sidebar card" was wrong — `sidebarCard(trailingMargin: 2)` pads *outside* the card.) |
| Yield order under width pressure | ≥420pt: full label + all actions. 280–419pt: drop the Open-in chevron, then the project segment of the label. <280pt: collapse the action group into a "…" menu. |
| Never collapses | the remove-from-split ✕ — the way out of a cramped split must not be the thing that gets squeezed out |

## States that must be specified

| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Zero terminal tabs | header present; "No terminal" empty state gains the card's gutter (§3) |
| Missing directory (solo **and** split) | header + warning triangle + **no** Open-in; unavailable view as an overlay, not a structural branch |
| Project root pane | `house` glyph, project name only, no "Workroom" a11y prefix; run + Open-in still apply |
| No editor installed | `OpenInControl` renders nothing; reserved width holds the layout |
| No run command configured | `RunControls` renders nothing; reserved width holds |
| Creating (focused) | chrome-less by decision — the setup dialog owns the pane (§6) |
| Window not key | card fill goes neutral (C3) |
| Narrow pane | the yield order above |
| Same workroom, two windows | "focus the owner" instead of a second Run (§5) |
| Reduce motion / transparency, light theme | no new animation is added; check `accent @ 0.10` contrast on a light theme manually |

---

## Verification

**Build gate** — `make app-*` must run with the command sandbox **disabled**:

```bash
make app-format && make app-lint && make app-build && make app-test
```

Read pass/fail from the `.xcresult` via `xcresulttool` (`make app-test` hides the summary under
Xcode 26). No files are added or removed, so no `xcodegen` surprises.

**Unit tests** (`WorkroomAppTests`)

- `RunCommandTests`: `runOrFocusRunCommand(for:)` acts on the **passed** target while a *different*
  target is selected (start / focus-existing / stopped→re-run / single-owner-elsewhere hop); the
  overload does **not** consult `isEditingTextField` (positive test: a focused field must not
  suppress it); the selection overload still delegates. `RunCommandTests.swift:225-243` currently
  drives the `runOwner` path through the selection — re-point it at the passed target.
- New: `WorkroomPaneToolbarPresentation` (shows-open-in / shows-run / shows-close matrix).
- `WorkroomLabelTests.swift:88` must keep passing (`WorkroomSplitTitlePresentation` survives).
- **Delete** `TabReorderMathTests.swift:162-176`
  (`testCompactLeadingInsetFitsARunTheSoloInsetDoesNot`) or fold it into the general `pinsControls`
  tests — with `compact` gone, `leadingInset: 8` is unreachable in production and the test keeps
  passing against literals while guarding nothing.

**UI tests** (`WorkroomAppUITests`, own scheme). Scope with
`xcodebuild -only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/<Class>/<method>` — `make app-uitest` ignores
`APP_TEST_FLAGS`. **Never run the whole suite.**

Must fix:
- `SplitPaneUITests.swift:198` — `assertCount(titlebars(app), reaches: 0)` is an exact `count == 0`
  and **will fail**. Change to `reaches: 1` **and** add
  `XCTAssertTrue(app.buttons["workroom.pane.close"].waitForNonExistence(timeout: 6))`, or the test
  loses all power to tell "collapsed" from "still split".
  (`:294-296` was suspected too — verified safe: `rootTitleBar` matches labels *without* "workroom",
  and no root pane renders at that point.)

Must add (default fixture = solo unless noted):
1. **The V1 guard, as a click:** solo `runCommand.run` and `openIn.primary` are **hittable and
   actually fire** — not merely `.exists`. Clicks are drivable from XCUITest even though hover is
   not, and this is the difference between the feature working and shipping two dead buttons.
2. Solo `.contextMenu` still opens (right-click the header → "Close" present) — the mask's effect on
   `.contextMenu` is undocumented.
3. Solo header drag 40pt creates **no** split (`titlebars` stays 1, `workroom.pane.close` never
   appears).
4. `workroom.pane.titlebar` exists with no split flags; `workroom.pane.close` does **not** solo but
   **does** with `-WorkroomUITestWorkroomSplit 1`.
5. `runCommand.run` is inside the pane — scope the query to the `workroom.pane` element, so it fails
   if the button were still in the titlebar.
6. `-WorkroomUITestWorkroomCount 3 -WorkroomUITestWorkroomSplit 1` → **two** `runCommand.run`
   buttons, one per member (the per-member point of the change).
7. Identity label `frame.width` unchanged across a run start (the reserved-width guard).
8. Frame assertion on `workroom.pane` locking the 6+4 geometry.
9. `openIn.primary` / `openIn.menu` exist and the menu lists ≥1 editor — first coverage for it.

Re-run: `SplitPaneUITests`, `RunStatusUITests`, **`TerminalAgentUITests`** (depends on
`runCommand.run` at `:31`), `RunSettingsPromptUITests`, `WorkroomWorkflowUITests`,
`TabActionsUITests`, `TabStripOverflowUITests` (`testChromeGlyphButtonsClaimTheirWholeWell` — the
strip's leading inset changed), `WindowDragUITests`, `MultiWindowTests` (V13).

Note: the singleton queries in `RunStatusUITests:33`, `TerminalAgentUITests:31` and
`WorkroomWorkflowUITests:143-159` now assume "one Run button per window" — any future split fixture
breaks `XCTAssertFalse(run.exists)`. Scope them to a pane element or accept the churn deliberately.
`WorkroomWorkflowUITests.swift:138-140`'s "collapses them into the toolbar overflow" rationale
becomes factually wrong — fix the comment.

**Manual (real mouse — required)**

Launch with `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1` under a **throwaway `$HOME`** so the real
`~/.config/workroom/config.json` and the Dev defaults domain are never touched. Drive via System
Events menu clicks, not blind keystrokes.

1. Solo: header present, accent-tinted card, run + Open-in right, **no** ✕. Hover each button — the
   well must light (real-mouse-only bug class: `macapp-textselection-swallows-taps`,
   `macapp-hover-slide-release-only`). **Click each** — they must fire (V1).
2. Right-click the header's **trailing** area — the workroom context menu must still appear.
3. Split into two: each header carries its own run + Open-in + ✕. Configure a run command, press Run
   on the **non-focused** member — the run starts in *that* workroom and the member is raised.
4. Collapse to solo via ✕: the survivor's terminal must not blank or re-parent. Note the ✕ + divider
   leaving shifts the action block right by ~27pt — that is expected, not a regression.
5. Drag a chip from the titlebar into the solo pane — the drop preview must appear **before** the
   split happens, including a drop inside the new 6pt gutter (the §6 hit-test fix).
6. Drag a 3-way split narrow and check the yield order; the ✕ must stay hit-testable at minimum width.
7. Drag a divider while watching for jank — the ratio is now local `@State` until mouse-up.
8. Titlebar: run/Open-in gone; ⌘R, ⇧⌘R, ⌥⌘R, ⇧⌘O and their menu items still act on the selection.
   Click Run with the sidebar filter focused — it must fire now.
9. Deactivate the window: the accent tint goes neutral.
10. Light theme: check the card fill is still legible against the terminal.
11. Missing directory: **not reachable via a split drop** — `insertWorkroomSplit` refuses a missing
    workroom (`AppStore+WorkroomSplit.swift:151-155`). Repro by deleting a member's directory *after*
    the group forms, and separately by deleting a solo workroom's directory (the §6 path).

---

## Appendix — review provenance

Four voices ran: Codex (CEO, design) and Claude subagents (CEO, eng), plus two supporting audits of
the `compact`/run-command surface and the existing per-workroom chrome. The eng pass was tasked to
**verify or refute** six specific claims about the draft, defaulting to REFUTED without evidence —
five confirmed, one half-refuted (`SplitPaneUITests:294-296` is safe). Every confirmed defect is
folded into the sections above rather than listed separately.

Rejected recommendations, recorded so they are not re-litigated: use `tabToolbar` instead of a header
(C1); suppress the solo label (C2); drop the solo card/accent (C3, accessibility half accepted);
unify on `TabToolbarButton` (C4). Also rejected as scope creep: ⌃Tab pane-focus cycling, a
`Defaults` toggle for the header, and moving branch/VCS state into the header (`TerminalStatusBar`
already shows branch and run state per pane at `TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104,129-175`).

Competitive note for the record: none of Ghostty, Warp, iTerm2, VS Code or Zed ships a per-pane
run/build action bar, and iTerm2's per-pane title bars are a per-profile preference off by default.
This is a deliberate divergence, not an oversight.

No per-phase `tasks-*.jsonl` files exist for this branch (the review skills ran as inline voices, not
as their own skills), so there is no aggregated task list beyond the implementation sections above.

# Issue #139 — Always show the workroom title bar and toolbar

## Context

Today a workroom only gets its own chrome when it is part of a **split group**. `WorkroomPaneLeaf`
(`macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:140`) gates a header + card underlay behind
`multi` (`leaves.count >= 2`, line 51): a `project / workroom` title bar with the remove-from-split
✕, and a rounded, tinted, shadowed card beneath the whole pane. A solo workroom gets none of it —
its terminal tab strip sits bare at the top of the detail area.

Meanwhile the workroom's own actions live in the **window titlebar**: `TrailingTitlebarBar`
(`Views/TitlebarBars.swift:162-169`) renders `OpenInControl` + `RunControls` keyed on
`store.selectedTarget`. That is the wrong home twice over:

- **Workroom-scoped controls in window-scoped chrome.** In a split every visible member has a path
  and a run state, but only the *selected* one is reachable.
- **`store.runOrFocusRunCommand()` reads the selection**, so a per-member Run button would start the
  run in the wrong workroom. That is a real semantic bug, not just placement.

Outcome: every workroom, split or not, renders as a self-contained card with its own title bar and
its own trailing toolbar; the window titlebar keeps only global chrome. Because the header becomes
unconditional, `WorkroomPaneLeaf` **loses** most of its `multi` branching rather than gaining more —
with no `if multi` there is no `_ConditionalContent` branch to flip when a split dissolves, so the
libghostty re-parent hazard on that axis disappears outright.

## Decisions of record

| # | Decision | Note |
|---|----------|------|
| D1 | Header always on; run + Open-in leave the titlebar **entirely** and become per-workroom; titlebar keeps sidebar toggle, back/forward, workroom chips, update pill, Quick Terminal | confirmed |
| D2 | Solo card geometry **identical** to a split member — 6pt outer gutter + 4pt inset | confirmed; makes `compact` genuinely dead |
| D3 | Solo renders accent-tinted (as a focused member) | confirmed, **+ key-window awareness** (see C3 below) |
| D4 | Header toolbar keeps `ToolbarIconButtonStyle` | confirmed, **+ both toolbars' trailing edges aligned by frame** (C4) |

Four cross-model challenges were raised at the gate and resolved:

| # | Challenge | Outcome |
|---|-----------|---------|
| C1 | Use the existing `tabToolbar` instead of a new header row | **Rejected.** The header is the container workroom UI grows into; the 28pt cost is deliberate. |
| C2 | Don't repeat the chip's label solo | **Rejected.** The chip can scroll out of an overflowing tab bar; the header is the pane's reliable identity. |
| C3 | Don't tint the solo card accent | **Rejected, with the accessibility half accepted:** the tint goes neutral when the window is not key. Light-theme contrast of `accent @ 0.10` is on the manual checklist. |
| C4 | Unify on `TabToolbarButton` | **Rejected, with the alignment half accepted:** keep the style, align both toolbars' trailing edges by hit-target frame and assert it. |

## The shape of the change

```
BEFORE                                    AFTER
window titlebar                           window titlebar
 ├ sidebar toggle, back/fwd                ├ sidebar toggle, back/fwd
 ├ workroom tab chips                      ├ workroom tab chips
 └ update · OpenIn · Run · QuickTerm       └ update · QuickTerm

| Yield order under width pressure | ≥420pt: full label + all actions. 280–419pt: drop the Open-in chevron, then the project segment of the label. <280pt: collapse the action group into a "…" menu. |

# Issue #139 — Always show the workroom title bar and toolbar

## Context

Today a workroom only gets its own chrome when it is part of a **split group**. `WorkroomPaneLeaf`
(`macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:140`) gates a header + card underlay behind
`multi` (`leaves.count >= 2`, line 51): a `project / workroom` title bar with the remove-from-split
✕, and a rounded, tinted, shadowed card beneath the whole pane. A solo workroom gets none of it —
its terminal tab strip sits bare at the top of the detail area.

Meanwhile the workroom's own actions live in the **window titlebar**: `TrailingTitlebarBar`
(`Views/TitlebarBars.swift:162-169`) renders `OpenInControl` + `RunControls` keyed on
`store.selectedTarget`. That is the wrong home twice over:

- **Workroom-scoped controls in window-scoped chrome.** In a split every visible member has a path
  and a run state, but only the *selected* one is reachable.
- **`store.runOrFocusRunCommand()` reads the selection**, so a per-member Run button would start the
  run in the wrong workroom. That is a real semantic bug, not just placement.

Outcome: every workroom, split or not, renders as a self-contained card with its own title bar and
its own trailing toolbar; the window titlebar keeps only global chrome. Because the header becomes
unconditional, `WorkroomPaneLeaf` **loses** most of its `multi` branching rather than gaining more —
with no `if multi` there is no `_ConditionalContent` branch to flip when a split dissolves, so the
libghostty re-parent hazard on that axis disappears outright.

## Decisions of record

| # | Decision | Note |
|---|----------|------|
| D1 | Header always on; run + Open-in leave the titlebar **entirely** and become per-workroom; titlebar keeps sidebar toggle, back/forward, workroom chips, update pill, Quick Terminal | confirmed |
| D2 | Solo card geometry **identical** to a split member — 6pt outer gutter + 4pt inset | confirmed; makes `compact` genuinely dead |
| D3 | Solo renders accent-tinted (as a focused member) | confirmed, **+ key-window awareness** (see C3 below) |
| D4 | Header toolbar keeps `ToolbarIconButtonStyle` | confirmed, **+ both toolbars' trailing edges aligned by frame** (C4) |

Four cross-model challenges were raised at the gate and resolved:

| # | Challenge | Outcome |
|---|-----------|---------|
| C1 | Use the existing `tabToolbar` instead of a new header row | **Rejected.** The header is the container workroom UI grows into; the 28pt cost is deliberate. |
| C2 | Don't repeat the chip's label solo | **Rejected.** The chip can scroll out of an overflowing tab bar; the header is the pane's reliable identity. |
| C3 | Don't tint the solo card accent | **Rejected, with the accessibility half accepted:** the tint goes neutral when the window is not key. Light-theme contrast of `accent @ 0.10` is on the manual checklist. |
| C4 | Unify on `TabToolbarButton` | **Rejected, with the alignment half accepted:** keep the style, align both toolbars' trailing edges by hit-target frame and assert it. |

## The shape of the change

```
BEFORE                                    AFTER
window titlebar                           window titlebar
 ├ sidebar toggle, back/fwd                ├ sidebar toggle, back/fwd
 ├ workroom tab chips                      ├ workroom tab chips
 └ update · OpenIn · Run · QuickTerm       └ update · QuickTerm

detail (solo)          detail (split)     detail (solo AND split — one shape)
┌──────────────────┐   ┌──────┐┌──────┐   ┌────────────────────────────────┐
│ [tab][tab] +  ⧈ ⧉│   │ hdr ✕││ hdr ✕│   │ ⬛ project / room   ⏵ ⧉  [✕]  │ ← always, 28pt
│ ░░ terminal ░░░░ │   │[tab] ││[tab] │   ├────────────────────────────────┤
└──────────────────┘   │ ░░░░ ││ ░░░░ │   │ [tab][tab] +          ⧈ ⧉ ⊠   │
  no card, 2pt gutter  └──────┘└──────┘   │ ░░░ terminal ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ │
                        cards, 6+4        └────────────────────────────────┘
                                            card + 6pt outer / 4pt inset
                                            [✕] = remove-from-split, multi only
```

`multi` survives in exactly **four** leaf-level places, none structural for the terminal: the ✕, the
context menu's "Remove from Split" item, the group-drag gesture mask, and the a11y `.isSelected`
trait.

**Cost, stated deliberately:** in-content chrome above the terminal goes 30pt → 58pt solo (+93%);
split members already pay ~62pt, so solo converges on split. Terminal loses 4pt per side.

---

## Implementation

### 1. `Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift` — the header becomes unconditional

**`WorkroomPaneLeaf.body` (140-218).** Drop the `if multi` around the header (150). **Keep the
`VStack(spacing: 0) { titleBar; content }` shape exactly** — the comment at 140-148 is load-bearing;
the header must stay a sibling above `content`, never a wrapper.

- **Gesture mask — `.subviews`, never `.none`.**
  `.gesture(dragGesture, including: multi ? .all : .subviews)`.
  `GestureMask.none` disables **all gestures in the subview hierarchy including the added one**, so
  `.none` would ship the solo pane's Run and Open-in buttons **dead** — and hover would still light
  their wells (`ToolbarIconButtonStyle` uses `.onHover`, not a gesture), so they would look alive.
  There is no `GestureMask` precedent anywhere in the app to catch this. Its effect on the sibling
  `.contextMenu` and on the AppKit `Menu` popup is undocumented — **prove both by real click.**
- `.contextMenu` (182-186) stays attached always: pass `onRemoveFromSplit: multi ? onClose : nil`;
  `workroomContextMenu` already omits the item and its divider on `nil`
  (`Views/WorkroomContextMenu.swift:37,50`). Scope the menu's `.contentShape` to the **leading label
  region** and attach the same menu to the trailing group, so right-click doesn't become positional
  guesswork once the bar's right half is buttons.
- **Card modifiers (196-213): delete every `multi ?` ternary.** `panel`, `cornerRadius: 8`, the
  focused/unfocused shadow, and `EdgeInsets(4,4,4,4)` become unconditional. Solo is *always* the
  selected leaf, so `focused` is already `true` — D3's accent needs no special case.
- **Key-window awareness (C3).** Extract the fill into a small child view
  `WorkroomPaneCardBackground(focused:)` that reads `@Environment(\.controlActiveState)` and returns
  `splitGroupFocusedFill` only when the window is key, `splitGroupFill` otherwise. As a child, it
  absorbs the activation churn on its own — the leaf and the terminal subtree below never
  re-evaluate for it. (Same invalidation reasoning as `RunControls` below.)
- `content(compact: multi)` (190) → `content()`; see §3.
- **Make the missing-directory choice non-structural.** Once §6 routes solo-missing through this
  leaf, the `if target.isMissing` at 236-256 can flip **in place under a live pane** — the exact
  hazard 140-148 warns about, which solo could never hit before. Always mount
  `TargetTerminalDetail` and draw the "Directory not found" `ContentUnavailableView` as an
  **overlay** over it. Update the 140-148 comment: the header is no longer the only such hazard.
- `.accessibilityAddTraits(focused && multi ? .isSelected : [])` (217): **keep the `multi` term.**
  Solo has nothing to select between, and this trait tracks *model* focus, not first responder —
  widening it would make every solo pane report selected and break how tests read it.

**`WorkroomSplitView.body` (83).** `.padding(.horizontal, multi ? 6 : 0)` → a named
`static let outerGutter: CGFloat = 6`, applied unconditionally. §6 must subtract it from the
drop hit-test.

**`WorkroomSplitDivider` — hold the live ratio locally.** `onChanged` currently calls
`onSetRatio` per mouse-move tick → `store.setWorkroomSplitRatio` writes `@Published workroomSplits`
→ `RootView` re-evaluates → **every leaf rebuilds at mouse-move rate.** With the header now doing
real work per pane, that becomes a hot path. Track the live ratio in `WorkroomSplitView` `@State` and
commit once on `.onEnded` — exactly the pattern `SidebarColumn.swift:22-24,47-62` already uses
("so each mouse-moved tick re-renders just this column, not the whole RootView tree").

**`WorkroomSplitGroupTitleBar` (264-317) → rename `WorkroomPaneTitleBar`** (no longer split-specific).
Props become `target: TerminalTarget`, `projectPath: String?`, `workroomName: String?`,
`focused: Bool`, `multi: Bool`, `onClose`, `onFocus`. Pass `projectPath` (the leaf already computes
`AppStore.projectPath(of: sid)` for `projectLabel`) rather than `sid` — one lookup, and no
`SidebarID` dependency in a presentation view. Derive `projectLabel` from it; drop the redundant
`isMissing` prop (`target.isMissing`). Keep
`accessibilityIdentifier("workroom.pane.titlebar")` — six `SplitPaneUITests` tests query it.

- **Glyph by kind:** `workroomName == nil` means a project root → `house`, matching the chip
  (`WorkroomTabBar.swift:487`); `cube` otherwise. Drop the `"Workroom "` a11y prefix for roots.
  Rare today (split-only); unconditional it is *every* root pane.
- **Trailing run:**

```swift
Spacer(minLength: 8)
HStack(spacing: 6) {
  if !target.isMissing {
    OpenInControl(path: target.path)
    if let projectPath { RunControls(target: target, projectPath: projectPath, onFocus: onFocus) }
  }
}
.frame(width: Self.actionsWidth, alignment: .trailing)   // reserved — see §5 / responsive contract
.buttonStyle(ToolbarIconButtonStyle())
if multi {
  TitlebarDivider()
  CloseWorkroomPaneButton(action: onClose)   // brings its own .plain style
}
```

- **`RunControls`' `@EnvironmentObject var store` is safe here.** SwiftUI invalidates only the view
  that declares the dependency, so it does **not** subscribe `WorkroomPaneLeaf` or the terminal
  subtree — the invariant at `WorkroomSplitView.swift:23-26,124-127` holds.
  `TargetTerminalDetail.swift:20` already reads the same environment object inside this leaf, so this
  is established practice.
- **Extract a pure `WorkroomPaneToolbarPresentation`** (`showsOpenIn` / `showsRun` / `showsClose`
  from `isMissing` / `hasRunCommand` / `multi`) beside `WorkroomSplitTitlePresentation` (112-118), so
  the trailing block is unit-testable without instantiating a view. `WorkroomSplitTitlePresentation`
  must survive — `WorkroomAppTests/WorkroomLabelTests.swift:88` tests it.
- **Hover** must be live for `ToolbarIconButtonStyle` and the `Menu`. The detail sits inside the
  `NavigationSplitView` that exists precisely to keep `.onHover` working near the top of the content
  (`RootView.swift:174-184`, issue #114). Verify with a **real mouse** — synthetic events lie here.

### 2. `Core/AppStore.swift` — Run must act on the passed target

```swift
/// ⌘R / menu: act on the current selection. Suppressed while a text field is being edited.
func runOrFocusRunCommand() {
  guard !isEditingTextField, let target = selectedTarget else { return }
  runOrFocusRunCommand(for: target)
}

/// The per-target state machine (the diagram at 1603-1629 moves here). A workroom's own Run
/// button calls this directly with ITS target.
func runOrFocusRunCommand(for target: TerminalTarget) {
  guard !target.isMissing else { return }
  … existing switch body, unchanged …
}
```

`isEditingTextField` stays on the **selection wrapper only**. That is deliberate and fixes a latent
bug: today a Run *click* while the sidebar filter or the Project Settings command field holds focus
silently no-ops, because the guard was written for ambient ⌘R (its own comment at 1593-1597 says so).
`stopRunCommand(for:)` (1711) and `restartRunCommand(for:)` (1726) already take a target and carry no
such guard, so all three buttons become consistent. Leave `toggleRunCommand(for:)` (1583, the sidebar
row toggle) alone — different semantics.

**Raise the member on the focus branches.** `.running(_, false)`/`.restarting` calls
`terminals.focus(tab, for: target)`, which switches *that member's* active tab **without** focusing
the member — and a non-focused member renders `surfaceActive: false` and is dimmed, so pressing Run
there looks like nothing happened. Thread the leaf's `onFocus` through `RunControls` and call it
before acting, or set `selectedTargetID` in the overload when the target is a visible member.

### 3. Delete the `compact` axis (D2 makes it dead)

With solo and split geometry identical, `compact` is permanently `true`. Remove it and inline the
values — a live-looking branch that can only take one value is worse than none:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:190,235` | `content(compact:)` → `content()` |
| `Views/TargetTerminalDetail.swift:19,27` | drop `var compact` + the pass-through |
| `Views/WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:21,59-60,86` | drop `var compact`; padding becomes `.horizontal, 2` / `.bottom, 2` |
| `Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:24,63` | drop `var compact`; `leadingInset` becomes `4` |

Rewrite the comments those numbers carry (they explain the solo-vs-split difference) to state the
single rule. Two adjacent fixes while in these files:

- **`WorkroomTerminalsView`: move the gutter padding onto the outer `Group`.** The zero-tab
  "No terminal" `ContentUnavailableView` (62-74) sits *outside* the `.padding` at 59-61, so inside a
  card it would render with no inset.
- **Fix the false invariant at 131-139.** The comment claims "this view mounts only in the
  single-workroom path" — already untrue for every split member, and this change edits those lines.

### 4. `Views/TitlebarBars.swift` — the titlebar loses the workroom controls

Delete the `if let target = store.selectedTarget, !target.isMissing { … }` block (162-169) with its
`OpenInControl`, `RunControls`, and trailing `TitlebarDivider`. What remains: the update pill (+ its
divider) and Quick Terminal. Update the doc comment (140-143), which advertises "the selected
target's run/open-in actions". **Check the resulting spacing** — with no update pending the trailing
bar becomes a lone button, and this change removes a group divider.

**Nothing else moves.** The Run menu (`WorkroomApp.swift:939-949`), Go ▸ "Open in …" (1082-1086), the
`AppDelegate` ⌘R/⌥⌘R/⇧⌘R monitor (267-288), and the `hasRunCommand`/`canOpenInEditor`
`focusedSceneValue`s keep acting on the selection through the unchanged selection-scoped entry
points. The keyboard path to a non-focused member stays "focus the pane, then ⌘R" — accepted; no new
shortcuts.

### 5. `Views/TargetDetailToolbar.swift` — ids, layout stability, multi-window

- **Accessibility ids.** `OpenInControl` has none today (only dynamic labels), which is why it has
  zero UI coverage. Add `openIn.primary` and `openIn.menu` (dotted convention). `RunControls` keeps
  `runCommand.run` / `.stop` / `.restart` verbatim — six existing tests query them.
- **Reserve the trailing width.** `RunControls` renders 1 button idle and 2 running, and nothing when
  `canRunCommand` is false; `OpenInControl` renders nothing with no editor installed. That is a ~28pt
  swing at run start, which moves the identity label's truncation point mid-run. Give the group a
  fixed reserved width (Stop+Restart's) or cross-fade the two states in a `ZStack`. In-repo
  precedent: `WorkroomTabBar.swift:202-212` toggles **opacity, not presence**, for exactly this.
- **Multi-window.** `runStates` is per-store, so window B renders `Run` while window A renders
  `Stop` for the same workroom — two adjacent contradictory buttons once this is per-pane. Read
  `WindowRegistry.shared.runOwner(for:excluding:)` too and render the not-mine-but-running case as a
  "focus the owner" affordance, not a Run button that silently teleports the user.
- Update both doc comments (9-14, 67-71): the host is the workroom pane title bar now.

### 6. `Views/RootView.swift` — close the two "no header" holes, fix the hit-test

- **Delete the `if target.isMissing` branch (584-590).** A solo missing workroom never reaches
  `WorkroomSplitView` today, so "always" was false. `target(for:)` returns a target even when the
  directory is gone, so deleting this routes it through `workroomSplitBody` → `.leaf(selected)` →
  the leaf, which renders the identical `ContentUnavailableView` (see §1's non-structural overlay).
- **Creation slot (577-582):** `isCreationFocused` bypasses the pane, while a *non-focused* creating
  member **does** get a header — "pixel-identical" breaks in the opposite direction from the missing
  case. **Decision: leave the creating slot chrome-less** (the setup dialog owns that moment) and say
  so in the comment; the premise reads "every workroom with a mounted pane", not "every state".
- **Subtract the gutter in the drop math.** `workroomChipDropTarget` (556-563) plans against the
  **unpadded** `detailContentFrame`, while the renderer plans *inside* `.padding(.horizontal, 6)`.
  Solo is pixel-exact today (0 padding); unconditional 6pt makes every drop 6pt off — a drop in the
  gutter is contained by RootView's rect (so it splits) but not by the pane rect (so **no** preview
  showed first). Subtract `WorkroomSplitView.outerGutter` in `workroomChipLocal`/`workroomChipDropTarget`.
- **Dead code, adjacent to these edits:** delete the never-called `titlebarBar` (63-89) and
  `workroomSplitBody`'s unreachable `else` branch (`selectedTarget` is
  `selectedTargetID.flatMap(target(for:))`, so a non-nil target implies a non-nil id).
- Add a no-op guard to `selectWorkroomTab` (570-573) — the solo header's focus tap now fires on
  every header click and rewrites unchanged selection state, publishing a whole-tree re-render.

### 7. `Core/ExternalEditor.swift` — cache the lookup before it goes per-pane

`ExternalEditor.installed` (19-26) is an **uncached computed property** doing 3
`NSWorkspace.urlForApplication(withBundleIdentifier:)` LaunchServices lookups; `icon` (47-51) calls
`NSWorkspace.icon(forFile:)` **and mutates the returned image's `size`** (shared-state mutation on an
image `NSWorkspace` may hand out from its own cache). Today that runs once per window; after this it
runs once per visible pane, on every mount, selection change, focus change and run-state change.
Back `installed` and the icons with a static cache invalidated on
`NSWorkspace.didLaunchApplicationNotification` / `didTerminateApplicationNotification`, and copy the
image before resizing. Worth doing regardless of this issue.

---

## Responsive contract (the numbers, stated once)

Both review voices named the missing width policy as the ambiguity that would do the most lasting
damage — every developer and test would otherwise encode a different assumption.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Header height | 28pt (unchanged) |
| Identity label cap | **180pt**, matching the chip's `maxTitleWidth` (`WorkroomTabBar.swift:410`) |
| Trailing group | fixed reserved width = Stop+Restart's, so the label's truncation point is a function of pane width only |
| Toolbar trailing edge | **both** the header's group and `tabToolbar` terminate 4pt from the card's inner trailing edge, aligned by **hit-target frame** (C4) — asserted, not eyeballed |
| Card geometry | 6pt outer gutter + 4pt inset all round → card edge sits **8pt** from the sidebar card; terminal at 14pt. (Today: terminal at 10pt. The draft's "10pt to the sidebar card" was wrong — `sidebarCard(trailingMargin: 2)` pads *outside* the card.) |
| Yield order under width pressure | ≥420pt: full label + all actions. 280–419pt: drop the Open-in chevron, then the project segment of the label. <280pt: collapse the action group into a "…" menu. |
| Never collapses | the remove-from-split ✕ — the way out of a cramped split must not be the thing that gets squeezed out |

## States that must be specified

| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Zero terminal tabs | header present; "No terminal" empty state gains the card's gutter (§3) |
| Missing directory (solo **and** split) | header + warning triangle + **no** Open-in; unavailable view as an overlay, not a structural branch |
| Project root pane | `house` glyph, project name only, no "Workroom" a11y prefix; run + Open-in still apply |
| No editor installed | `OpenInControl` renders nothing; reserved width holds the layout |
| No run command configured | `RunControls` renders nothing; reserved width holds |
| Creating (focused) | chrome-less by decision — the setup dialog owns the pane (§6) |
| Window not key | card fill goes neutral (C3) |
| Narrow pane | the yield order above |
| Same workroom, two windows | "focus the owner" instead of a second Run (§5) |
| Reduce motion / transparency, light theme | no new animation is added; check `accent @ 0.10` contrast on a light theme manually |

---

## Verification

**Build gate** — `make app-*` must run with the command sandbox **disabled**:

```bash
make app-format && make app-lint && make app-build && make app-test
```

Read pass/fail from the `.xcresult` via `xcresulttool` (`make app-test` hides the summary under
Xcode 26). No files are added or removed, so no `xcodegen` surprises.

**Unit tests** (`WorkroomAppTests`)

- `RunCommandTests`: `runOrFocusRunCommand(for:)` acts on the **passed** target while a *different*
  target is selected (start / focus-existing / stopped→re-run / single-owner-elsewhere hop); the
  overload does **not** consult `isEditingTextField` (positive test: a focused field must not
  suppress it); the selection overload still delegates. `RunCommandTests.swift:225-243` currently
  drives the `runOwner` path through the selection — re-point it at the passed target.
- New: `WorkroomPaneToolbarPresentation` (shows-open-in / shows-run / shows-close matrix).
- `WorkroomLabelTests.swift:88` must keep passing (`WorkroomSplitTitlePresentation` survives).
- **Delete** `TabReorderMathTests.swift:162-176`
  (`testCompactLeadingInsetFitsARunTheSoloInsetDoesNot`) or fold it into the general `pinsControls`
  tests — with `compact` gone, `leadingInset: 8` is unreachable in production and the test keeps
  passing against literals while guarding nothing.

**UI tests** (`WorkroomAppUITests`, own scheme). Scope with
`xcodebuild -only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/<Class>/<method>` — `make app-uitest` ignores
`APP_TEST_FLAGS`. **Never run the whole suite.**

Must fix:
- `SplitPaneUITests.swift:198` — `assertCount(titlebars(app), reaches: 0)` is an exact `count == 0`
  and **will fail**. Change to `reaches: 1` **and** add
  `XCTAssertTrue(app.buttons["workroom.pane.close"].waitForNonExistence(timeout: 6))`, or the test
  loses all power to tell "collapsed" from "still split".
  (`:294-296` was suspected too — verified safe: `rootTitleBar` matches labels *without* "workroom",
  and no root pane renders at that point.)

Must add (default fixture = solo unless noted):
1. **The V1 guard, as a click:** solo `runCommand.run` and `openIn.primary` are **hittable and
   actually fire** — not merely `.exists`. Clicks are drivable from XCUITest even though hover is
   not, and this is the difference between the feature working and shipping two dead buttons.
2. Solo `.contextMenu` still opens (right-click the header → "Close" present) — the mask's effect on
   `.contextMenu` is undocumented.
3. Solo header drag 40pt creates **no** split (`titlebars` stays 1, `workroom.pane.close` never
   appears).
4. `workroom.pane.titlebar` exists with no split flags; `workroom.pane.close` does **not** solo but
   **does** with `-WorkroomUITestWorkroomSplit 1`.
5. `runCommand.run` is inside the pane — scope the query to the `workroom.pane` element, so it fails
   if the button were still in the titlebar.
6. `-WorkroomUITestWorkroomCount 3 -WorkroomUITestWorkroomSplit 1` → **two** `runCommand.run`
   buttons, one per member (the per-member point of the change).
7. Identity label `frame.width` unchanged across a run start (the reserved-width guard).
8. Frame assertion on `workroom.pane` locking the 6+4 geometry.
9. `openIn.primary` / `openIn.menu` exist and the menu lists ≥1 editor — first coverage for it.

Re-run: `SplitPaneUITests`, `RunStatusUITests`, **`TerminalAgentUITests`** (depends on
`runCommand.run` at `:31`), `RunSettingsPromptUITests`, `WorkroomWorkflowUITests`,
`TabActionsUITests`, `TabStripOverflowUITests` (`testChromeGlyphButtonsClaimTheirWholeWell` — the
strip's leading inset changed), `WindowDragUITests`, `MultiWindowTests` (V13).

Note: the singleton queries in `RunStatusUITests:33`, `TerminalAgentUITests:31` and
`WorkroomWorkflowUITests:143-159` now assume "one Run button per window" — any future split fixture
breaks `XCTAssertFalse(run.exists)`. Scope them to a pane element or accept the churn deliberately.
`WorkroomWorkflowUITests.swift:138-140`'s "collapses them into the toolbar overflow" rationale
becomes factually wrong — fix the comment.

**Manual (real mouse — required)**

Launch with `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1` under a **throwaway `$HOME`** so the real
`~/.config/workroom/config.json` and the Dev defaults domain are never touched. Drive via System
Events menu clicks, not blind keystrokes.

1. Solo: header present, accent-tinted card, run + Open-in right, **no** ✕. Hover each button — the
   well must light (real-mouse-only bug class: `macapp-textselection-swallows-taps`,
   `macapp-hover-slide-release-only`). **Click each** — they must fire (V1).
2. Right-click the header's **trailing** area — the workroom context menu must still appear.
3. Split into two: each header carries its own run + Open-in + ✕. Configure a run command, press Run
   on the **non-focused** member — the run starts in *that* workroom and the member is raised.
4. Collapse to solo via ✕: the survivor's terminal must not blank or re-parent. Note the ✕ + divider
   leaving shifts the action block right by ~27pt — that is expected, not a regression.
5. Drag a chip from the titlebar into the solo pane — the drop preview must appear **before** the
   split happens, including a drop inside the new 6pt gutter (the §6 hit-test fix).
6. Drag a 3-way split narrow and check the yield order; the ✕ must stay hit-testable at minimum width.
7. Drag a divider while watching for jank — the ratio is now local `@State` until mouse-up.
8. Titlebar: run/Open-in gone; ⌘R, ⇧⌘R, ⌥⌘R, ⇧⌘O and their menu items still act on the selection.
   Click Run with the sidebar filter focused — it must fire now.
9. Deactivate the window: the accent tint goes neutral.
10. Light theme: check the card fill is still legible against the terminal.
11. Missing directory: **not reachable via a split drop** — `insertWorkroomSplit` refuses a missing
    workroom (`AppStore+WorkroomSplit.swift:151-155`). Repro by deleting a member's directory *after*
    the group forms, and separately by deleting a solo workroom's directory (the §6 path).

---

## Appendix — review provenance

Four voices ran: Codex (CEO, design) and Claude subagents (CEO, eng), plus two supporting audits of
the `compact`/run-command surface and the existing per-workroom chrome. The eng pass was tasked to
**verify or refute** six specific claims about the draft, defaulting to REFUTED without evidence —
five confirmed, one half-refuted (`SplitPaneUITests:294-296` is safe). Every confirmed defect is
folded into the sections above rather than listed separately.

Rejected recommendations, recorded so they are not re-litigated: use `tabToolbar` instead of a header
(C1); suppress the solo label (C2); drop the solo card/accent (C3, accessibility half accepted);
unify on `TabToolbarButton` (C4). Also rejected as scope creep: ⌃Tab pane-focus cycling, a
`Defaults` toggle for the header, and moving branch/VCS state into the header (`TerminalStatusBar`
already shows branch and run state per pane at `TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104,129-175`).

Competitive note for the record: none of Ghostty, Warp, iTerm2, VS Code or Zed ships a per-pane
run/build action bar, and iTerm2's per-pane title bars are a per-profile preference off by default.
This is a deliberate divergence, not an oversight.

No per-phase `tasks-*.jsonl` files exist for this branch (the review skills ran as inline voices, not
as their own skills), so there is no aggregated task list beyond the implementation sections above.

Done. Build ✓, lint ✓, unit tests **1372 passed / 0 failed**.

## What shipped

Branch `feat/139-always-show-workroom-header`, uncommitted. 13 files changed, 2 added.

- **`WorkroomSplitView`** — header unconditional. `multi` now survives in only 4 leaf-level spots (✕, its menu item, the drag mask, the a11y trait). Card fill/radius/shadow/inset all unconditional. Divider ratio moved to local `@State`, commits on mouse-up.
- **`AppStore`** — `runOrFocusRunCommand(for:)` split out; `isEditingTextField` left on the selection door only. Per-target press raises its own pane.
- **`compact` deleted** across 4 files. `TitlebarBars` lost the workroom block. `RootView` lost the `isMissing` branch, the dead `titlebarBar`, and the unreachable `workroomSplitBody` else.
- **`ExternalEditor`** cached (3 LaunchServices lookups + icon per body eval, about to go per-pane).

## Verified

`.subviews` not `.none` for the gesture mask — the critical one. `testSoloRunButtonActuallyFires` clicks the button and requires Stop to replace Run, because a masked button still exists, is hittable, and lights its hover well.

## Not verified — and I can't

**The UI tests never ran.** `Timed out while enabling automation mode`. I confirmed it's the environment, not the code: an **untouched** test (`WorkroomsViewUITests/testActiveWorkroomShowsATab`) fails identically. Known wedge, needs a login-session reset. So the 7 new UI tests and the inverted `SplitPaneUITests:198` assertion are **written and compiling but unexecuted**.

The 11-step real-mouse checklist is also outstanding — synthetic events lie on this surface.

## Three deviations

1. **V13 not implemented** (per-pane "focus the owner" button when another window owns the run). It needs cross-store observation the app doesn't have, so a rendered state would go stale and mislead. The *action* is already correct — the owner hop happens at press time. Documented in `RunControls`; it's pre-existing and this change doesn't multiply it (each window shows a workroom once).
2. **Missing-directory state went inside `TargetTerminalDetail`'s ZStack**, not an overlay in the leaf. An overlay would still mount a terminal over a dead path — the exact thing the original branch existed to prevent. Same non-structural benefit, correct semantics.
3. `focusTargetPane` lives in the store rather than threaded through the view. The plan allowed either.

## Two things for your eye

- **Glyph centres still differ ~4.5pt** between the header toolbar and `tabToolbar`. Hit-target trailing edges align at 4pt as specified, but the well sizes differ (22pt vs ~19pt), so the glyphs can't also align. That's the residual of keeping both button styles (your D4).
- **Solo idle leaves ~34pt between Open-in and Run** — the width reserved for Restart, which is what keeps the label's truncation point stable. Reads as a group gap; may or may not sit right with you.
we have more space in header now, so make the button icons bigger. also fade them out when workroom is not focused - like the terminal toolbar buttons do.
Two edits: a roomier size variant for the header's buttons, and the same focus fade the terminal strip uses.

Done. Build ✓, lint ✓, **1372 passed / 0 failed**.

## Bigger icons

Added a `Size` variant to `ToolbarIconButtonStyle` — `.titlebar` (unchanged defaults) and `.paneHeader`:

| | titlebar | paneHeader |
|---|---|---|
| well | 22pt | **24pt** |
| glyph | inherits ambient | **15pt** |

24pt still clears the 28pt row with 2pt to spare. The window titlebar's own buttons take the default, so they're byte-identical to before.

Glyphs that size themselves don't get the style's font, so I tuned them at their call sites: editor icon 16→**18**, its chevron 8→**9**, `pip.exit` ✕ 10→**13**.

`RunControls.reservedWidth` now derives from `Size.paneHeader.footprint` instead of restating `22 + 3*2` — resizing the buttons can't leave a stale gap where Restart appears.

## Fade

`.opacity(focused ? 1 : 0.45)` + `easeInOut(0.07)`, `reduceMotion`-respecting — same values and curve as `WorkroomTerminalsView` uses on the tab strip, so header, strip and the per-pane scrim fade as one unit.

Applied to the whole trailing group including the divider and ✕. Opacity doesn't block hit-testing, so an unfocused member's ✕ stays clickable — that matters, it's the way out of a cramped split.

## One thing I changed my mind on mid-edit

I first wrote `.font(size.glyph.map { .system(size: $0) })`. `.font(nil)` **resets** to the system default rather than inheriting — so if any ancestor ever set a font, the titlebar buttons would silently shift. Replaced with an explicit branch; `size` is fixed per style instance so it never flips at runtime.

Still unverified: UI tests (automation subsystem wedged — reproduced on an untouched test) and the real-mouse pass. Revert clean — no `Size` variant left, window titlebar back to its original 22pt/ambient behaviour (the constants are just named now so `RunControls` derives its reserved width instead of restating `22 + 3*2`).

## The actual bug

Open-in wasn't small because the buttons differed — **all wells were already 22pt**. Three things were off:

| Glyph | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| run / stop / restart | ambient (13pt) | **13pt**, explicit |
| Open-in app icon | 16pt bitmap | **18pt** |
| Open-in chevron | 8pt | **13pt** |
| ✕ `pip.exit` | 10pt, **`.plain` + 8pt padding — no square well** | **13pt**, shared 22pt well |

The ✕ was the genuine odd one out: it styled itself, so it was the one control in the header whose well was a different size *and shape* from its neighbours. It now inherits the group's style like everything else.

Two constants, one place (`PaneToolbarIcon`), and the header sets them on the group so nothing restates a number.

## Why the app icon is 18 and not 13

Equal numbers there would be the wrong kind of equal. macOS app-icon artwork ships with transparent margin around it — roughly a fifth of the canvas — so at the symbols' point size it renders visibly smaller than they do. That's what you were looking at. 18pt is where it *looks* like its neighbours, which is the only size a user can see. The comment says exactly this so nobody "fixes" it to 13 later.

## One judgement call to check

The chevron went 8pt → 13pt, taking "all the same size" literally. It's a disclosure indicator rather than an action icon, and `HStack(spacing: -8)` was tuned to tuck an 8pt chevron against the editor icon — a 13pt one is ~60% wider, so that overlap may now read crowded. Say the word and I'll make it subordinate again (or loosen the spacing); I can't judge it without the screen.

**Divider added, and it hides properly.** The subtle part: `RunControls` renders *nothing* when no run command is configured, and `OpenInControl` renders nothing when no supported editor is installed — so the header couldn't see whether either group was actually there. A divider gated on "should there be run buttons" would have left a stray rule on a project with no run command.

Fixed by moving both facts into `WorkroomPaneToolbarPresentation` as inputs and deriving `divider = run && openIn` in the same pass. It now can't disagree with the buttons on either side. **Yes, the icon can be bigger — 18 → 20.** The 22pt well was never the constraint: `ToolbarIconButtonStyle` sets `minWidth`/`minHeight`, so the well grows with its label. The real ceiling is the title bar's 28pt row:

- **24pt** — 2pt clearance, safe
- **26pt** — 1pt, tight
- **>28pt** — clips, or the row has to grow

Above ~22pt the icon starts filling the hover well edge to edge, so the well stops reading as a well. I went to 20 for a visible bump with room left; the headroom is documented on the constant so the next person doesn't assume 22 is a cap. Say a number if you want it pushed further.

Build ✓, lint ✓, **1374 passed / 0 failed**.

## The frame was never sizing the icon

The control was built as a hidden SF Symbol with the real icon overlaid on it:

```swift
Image(systemName: "arrow.up.forward.app")
  .hidden()
  .overlay { Image(nsImage: remembered.icon)... }
  .frame(width: 20, height: 20)   // ← did nothing to the icon
```

An `.overlay` takes the size of the view it's attached to, and a bare `Image` is fixed-size — it reports its intrinsic size no matter what's proposed. So the icon rendered at whatever the ambient **font** made the hidden symbol (~13pt), and the `.frame` just centred that 13pt icon inside a larger transparent box.

Which means it was never 16, never 18, never 20. It's been ~13pt the whole time, and all three of my "bigger" edits changed a box nobody could see. That's on me — I changed the number and reported it without a way to confirm the number was load-bearing.

Fixed by sizing the icon itself:

```swift
Image(nsImage: remembered.icon)
  .renderingMode(.original)
  .resizable()
  .scaledToFit()
  .frame(width: PaneToolbarIcon.appIcon, height: PaneToolbarIcon.appIcon)
```

**It also explains the original complaint.** At 13pt, app-icon artwork carries ~20% transparent margin, so ~10pt of visible glyph sat next to 13pt symbols that fill their box. Genuinely much smaller, exactly as you said.

Now at 20pt it should be plainly bigger. Two numbers worth knowing, both now on the constant:

- **~16-17pt** = exact optical parity with the 13pt symbols (13 ÷ 0.8)
- **22pt** = the real ceiling. The well is a `minWidth`, so anything above 22 grows *this* button's well while the run buttons stay 22 — it'd become visibly taller than its neighbours

20 is deliberately past parity so it reads as the group's primary action. Say a number if you want it dialled back.

feat(macapp): give every workroom its own title bar and toolbar

Closes #139.

A workroom only had its own chrome when it was part of a split group, and its
run/"Open in…" controls lived in the window title bar keyed on the *selected*
target — so a co-displayed split member's were unreachable, and
`runOrFocusRunCommand()` read the selection, meaning a per-member Run button
would have started the run in the wrong workroom.

Now every workroom renders as a card with its own header and its own trailing
toolbar, and the window title bar keeps only window-level chrome (sidebar
toggle, back/forward, workroom chips, update pill, Quick Terminal).

Because the header became unconditional, `WorkroomPaneLeaf` LOST most of its
`multi` branching rather than gaining more: with no `if` there is no
`_ConditionalContent` branch left to flip when a split dissolves, so the
libghostty re-parent hazard on that axis is gone. `multi` now survives in four
leaf-level places only — the remove-from-split ✕, its menu item, the group-drag
gesture mask, and the a11y `.isSelected` trait.

Solo and split geometry are identical (6pt outer gutter + 4pt inset), which
made the `compact` parameter permanently true, so it is deleted across four
files. The card's accent tint goes neutral when the window isn't key.

Run is now per-target: `runOrFocusRunCommand(for:)` carries the state machine
and the selection-scoped overload delegates to it. `isEditingTextField` stays on
the selection door only, which also fixes a latent bug — a Run *click* while the
sidebar filter held focus used to no-op, because that guard was written for
ambient ⌘R. The button is shown even with no run command configured; pressing it
opens Project Settings with the warning, the same branch ⌘R has used since #127.

Notable fixes found while building it:

- `GestureMask.none` would have shipped dead buttons. The header carries the
  group-drag gesture, and `.none` disables every gesture in the SUBVIEW
  hierarchy as well as the added one — solo, that kills the header's own Run and
  Open-in. Hover is `.onHover`, not a gesture, so they would have looked alive.
  `.subviews` drops only the drag.
- A solo missing-directory workroom never reached `WorkroomSplitView` at all
  (`RootView` had its own `isMissing` branch), so "always" was false for it.
  `TargetTerminalDetail` now owns that state for every pane as a ZStack sibling,
  not a structural branch under a live surface.
- The "Open in…" icon ignored its own `.frame`: it was a hidden SF Symbol with
  the icon in an `.overlay`, and an overlay takes its base's size, so the icon
  rendered at whatever the ambient font made the symbol. It is sized directly now.
- `ExternalEditor.installed` was an uncached computed property doing three
  LaunchServices lookups per evaluation, about to run once per visible pane;
  `icon` mutated the size of an image `NSWorkspace` may share. Both cached, and
  the icon is drawn into a fresh image.
- Divider-drag ratios are held in local `@State` and committed on mouse-up
  instead of publishing to the store per mouse-moved tick, which rebuilt every
  pane at cursor rate.
- Chip-drop hit-testing planned against the unpadded detail rect while the
  renderer plans inside the gutter, so a drop in the gutter split with no preview.

`SplitPaneUITests` asserted a collapsed split leaves ZERO title bars; it now
leaves one, and the ✕ is what distinguishes collapsed from still-split.
`TabReorderMathTests`' compact-inset case no longer describes a distinction the
app makes, so it is restated as plain arithmetic.

Unit tests pass (1374). The new XCUITests are written but UNRUN: this machine's
automation subsystem is wedged ("Timed out while enabling automation mode"),
reproduced on an untouched test. The real-mouse pass is also outstanding — hover
and click on this bar are a known real-mouse-only bug class.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---
name: macapp-xcuitest-automation-wedge
description: XCUITest "Timed out while enabling automation mode" is a transient environment wedge, not a code failure — confirm with an untouched test, and retry later before resorting to a login-session reset.
metadata:
  type: project
---

macapp XCUITest runs can fail with `The test runner failed to initialize for UI testing.
(Underlying Error: Timed out while enabling automation mode.)`. This is the **automation
subsystem**, not the code: `make app-build` and `make app-test` (unit) keep passing, because they
never enter UI-testing automation mode.

**Diagnose it in one run:** re-run a test that your change did NOT touch (e.g.
`WorkroomAppUITests/WorkroomsViewUITests/testActiveWorkroomShowsATab`). Same error on an untouched
test ⇒ environment, so don't debug your diff.

**It can clear on its own.** Observed 2026-07-31: wedged for a stretch of a session, then every
XCUITest ran green later in the same session with no login-out, no reboot, nothing but elapsed
time and intervening builds. So **retry before escalating** — a login-session reset is the last
resort, not the first response. (An earlier version of this note said a reset was required; that
overstated it.)

Related: [[macapp-uitest-only-relevant-class]] for how to scope runs (`make app-uitest` ignores
`APP_TEST_FLAGS` — call `xcodebuild` with `-only-testing:<Class>[/<method>]`), and
[[macapp-xcuitest-gotchas]] for what is and isn't queryable.

Reading results: `** TEST SUCCEEDED **` alone is not proof anything ran — a run with zero tests
also succeeds, and an `XCTSkip` counts as neither pass nor fail. Get per-test verdicts from the
`.xcresult`:
`xcrun xcresulttool get test-results tests --path <…>.xcresult` and check each `Test Case` node's
`result`.

**`skippedTests` is the trap.** A `result: "Passed"` run with `failedTests: 0` can still be hiding a

the guard keyed on an element that wasn't queryable, silently retiring the assertion. Always check
